parameter_matrix.note: Wider operating Vin window supports broader rail & battery chemistry headroom.
Higher Vin,abs improves survivability against hot-plug and inductive bus spikes.
Tighter Vout tolerance improves ADC reference and digital rail margin.
Actual usable continuous Iout is also bounded by package θJA thermal derating.
Lower Iq directly extends sleep-mode battery life in always-on IoT/portable rails.
Lower dropout allows regulation deeper into Li-ion / 3.7 V discharge curves.
Non-ceramic-stable LDOs oscillate with low-ESR MLCCs unless series resistance or tantalum is used.
Higher PSRR attenuates upstream switching-converter ripple on analog/RF rails.
Critical for RF VCOs, low-noise ADCs, and precision sensor excitation.
Lower θJA yields lower junction temperature rise ΔTj = (Vin - Vout) × Iout × θJA.
Keep steady-state Tj at least 15–25 °C below Tj,max for production reliability.

swap_risks: CAUTION THERMAL MARGIN: Package θJA differs by 62% (LM1117IMPX-3.3/NOPB: 61.6 °C/W p.4 vs NCP1117ST33T3G: 160 °C/W p.2); re-check Tj = Ta + Pd × θJA against Tj,max.
BENCH VERIFICATION: Confirm thermal dissipation margin using θJA (LM1117IMPX-3.3/NOPB: 61.6 °C/W vs NCP1117ST33T3G: 160 °C/W) and worst-case ambient temperature (-40..125 °C vs 0..125 °C).
engineering_verdict: LM1117IMPX-3.3/NOPB (Texas Instruments, SOT-223-3) and NCP1117ST33T3G (onsemi, SOT-223-3) qualify as Level 1 Candidate Drop-In alternatives with matching pin assignments, compatible exposed-pad nets, and aligned core operating ratings. Key datasheet deltas: Iq is 5000 µA (p.8) vs 6000 µA (p.4), max output current is 800 mA (p.7) vs 1000 mA (p.3), recommended Vin,max is 15 V (p.4) vs 15 V (p.3), typical dropout is 1200 mV (p.8) vs 1070 mV (p.3), and ceramic capacitor stability is ESR-constrained vs ESR-constrained. Always validate pinout orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.1), thermal margin (θJA 61.6 vs 160 °C/W), and official manufacturer datasheets on hardware prototypes before production release.
